questions.text: Is the h_rdata value defined by the requirements to equal USR_ACCESSE2? (Scenario: A read of 0x004 (BUILD) occurs during reset assertion, while the MMCM is unlocked.) Two careful readers of the requirements disagree about this; what is the intended behaviour?

What value does the CRC register read (as a 32-bit integer in decimal)? (SCRATCH is 0 per spec; CRC state before any INIT is the question.) (Scenario: Right after rst deasserts following power-up, with no writes made, the host reads SCRATCH (0x008), CRC, BYTE_COUNT and BUSY_CYCLES.) The requirements do not say; what should happen?
questions.answer: 0 (CRC reads 0x00000000 after reset, since the internal state is 0xFFFFFFFF and the final XOR is applied on read; decimal 0)
questions.evidence: Reset: CRC state is the start value 0xFFFFFFFF internally, so CRC reads 0x00000000 for no bytes (the final XOR is applied on read); BYTE_COUNT 0, BUSY_CYCLES 0, TAIL_LEN 0, CTRL 0.

questions.text: What value does BUSY_CYCLES read? (Scenario: After INIT, 5 full words are pushed, then PUSH_N with TAIL_LEN 2 is pushed.) The requirements do not say; what should happen?
questions.answer: BUSY_CYCLES reads 6. The 5 PUSH4 pushes count one each, and the PUSH_N with TAIL_LEN 2 (N>0) counts one more.
questions.evidence: BUSY_CYCLES counts one per clock in which a push is processed (PUSH4 or PUSH_N with N>0), it is 32 bits and wraps; a PUSH_N with N = 0 does not count.

questions.text: What does SCRATCH read after reset deasserts? (Scenario: SCRATCH holds 0xDEADBEEF and 3 words have been pushed; rst is asserted for 8 clocks then deasserts.) Two careful readers of the requirements disagree about this; what is the intended behaviour?
questions.answer: SCRATCH reads 0 after reset. The spec says it resets to 0, so the earlier value 0xDEADBEEF is cleared when rst is asserted.
questions.evidence: | 0x008 | SCRATCH | RW | 32 bits, reads back what was written, resets to 0 |

questions.text: Is the 0x12345678 word included in the CRC and BYTE_COUNT after that clock? (Scenario: In the same clock, h_we writes CTRL with bit 0 = 1 (INIT) while a PUSH4 is also being accepted with data 0x12345678.) The requirements do not say; what should happen?
questions.answer: No. INIT wins over a push in the same clock, so the push is dropped. The 0x12345678 word is not included in the CRC or BYTE_COUNT, and after the clock the CRC state is back at the start value with BYTE_COUNT and BUSY_CYCLES at 0.
questions.evidence: INIT written takes effect in the clock after the write and clears CRC state, BYTE_COUNT and BUSY_CYCLES; it wins over a PUSH4 or PUSH_N in the same clock (the push is dropped).

questions.text: What value does h_rdata show within 2 clocks of that read? (Scenario: At clock t, h_we writes SCRATCH (0x008) with 0xA5A5A5A5, and h_re is also asserted at t with h_addr 0x008. SCRATCH previously held 0x11111111.) The requirements do not say; what should happen?

What does BYTE_COUNT read after reset deasserts? (Scenario: Reset asserts in the middle of a stream of consecutive PUSH4 words with BYTE_COUNT at 40; after reset deasserts no INIT is written.) The requirements do not say; what should happen?
questions.answer: BYTE_COUNT reads 0 after reset deasserts. Reset state is BYTE_COUNT 0, and no INIT is needed for that.
questions.evidence: Reset: CRC state is the start value 0xFFFFFFFF internally, so CRC reads 0x00000000 for no bytes (the final XOR is applied on read); BYTE_COUNT 0, BUSY_CYCLES 0, TAIL_LEN 0, CTRL 0.

questions.text: Please restate REQ-31 so that one statement can be checked: split it into one requirement per checkable statement, each with its own id and proof method

Does the CRC read equal zlib.crc32 of the empty message (0x00000000)? (Scenario: INIT and an accepted PUSH4 of 0xAABBCCDD occur in the same clock, then no other pushes. CRC is read afterward.) The requirements do not say; what should happen?
questions.answer: Yes. INIT wins over a PUSH4 or PUSH_N in the same clock and the push is dropped. The CRC state is therefore back at the start value, and CRC reads 0x00000000, the same as for an empty message (BYTE_COUNT and BUSY_CYCLES also stay 0).
questions.evidence: INIT written takes effect in the clock after the write and clears CRC state, BYTE_COUNT and BUSY_CYCLES; it wins over a PUSH4 or PUSH_N in the same clock (the push is dropped).

questions.text: What is the behaviour of the design for this tail length? (Scenario: PUSH_N is issued with a TAIL_LEN value of 4 (or greater than 3, if the field is wider than 2 bits), which is not among the specified 0 to 3 values.) The requirements do not say; what should happen?
questions.answer: A TAIL_LEN of 4 or more cannot be stored, because only bits 1:0 are kept. Writing 4 stores 0, so a following PUSH_N pushes nothing and BYTE_COUNT does not change. Writing 5, 6 or 7 stores 1, 2 or 3, and PUSH_N then pushes that many bytes.
questions.evidence: TAIL_LEN values above 3 cannot be written: the upper bits are ignored (only bits 1:0 are stored).

questions.text: Is the CRC equal to zlib.crc32 of those 4 bytes? (Scenario: After reset deasserts with no INIT written, a PUSH4 of 0x61626364 is issued (no INIT before it), then CRC is read.) The requirements do not say; what should happen?
questions.answer: Yes. Reset puts the CRC state at the start value 0xFFFFFFFF, so with no INIT the push behaves as if INIT had been issued. CRC then reads zlib.crc32 of the bytes in the order sent: 0x64, 0x63, 0x62, 0x61, least significant byte first.
questions.evidence: - Reset: CRC state is the start value 0xFFFFFFFF internally, so CRC reads 0x00000000 for no bytes (the final XOR is applied on read); BYTE_COUNT 0, BUSY_CYCLES 0, TAIL_LEN 0, CTRL 0.

questions.text: What is BYTE_COUNT after that clock? (Scenario: BYTE_COUNT is 16. h_we writes 0 to the BYTE_COUNT register address while a PUSH4 is accepted in the same clock.) The requirements do not say; what should happen?
questions.answer: The write to BYTE_COUNT (read-only) is ignored and has no effect on the counter. BYTE_COUNT changes only through pushes and INIT. The register port has a single h_we/h_addr, so a write to the BYTE_COUNT address cannot occur in the same clock as a PUSH4 write.
questions.evidence: Writes to read-only registers are ignored.

questions.text: What value does h_rdata show: old or new? (Scenario: At clock T, h_we writes 0x77 to SCRATCH and h_re reads SCRATCH in the same clock (old value 0x11).) The requirements do not say; what should happen?
